t: Applications of Programming in Real Life
tz: 编程在现实生活中的应用
sec: 8.5 Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Smart Living

cards.en:
Intuition: think of fixing a wobbly desk lamp yourself instead of buying a new one. A maker is someone who builds or changes things to solve their own problem.

The idea:

  • Maker culture = problem-solving through DIY (Do It Yourself).
  • Makers create or adapt products using raw materials and technology, e.g. robots, electronic sensors, 3D printing.
  • Tools are now cheap and programming is easy to learn, so people move from tool users to tool builders.
  • Makers usually build a prototype first. A prototype is an early working model used to test an idea before the final product.

Exam wording: Maker culture encourages problem-solving through DIY, creating or adapting products with raw materials and technology (robots, electronic sensors, 3D printing). A prototype is an early model built to test an idea.
cards.zh:
直觉：台灯坏了，自己动手修好，而不是买新的。Maker（创客）就是自己动手做或改东西来解决问题的人。

  • Maker culture = problem-solving through DIY（自己动手解决问题）。
  • 用原材料和科技去制作或改造产品，例如 robots、electronic sensors、3D printing。
  • 工具便宜、编程容易学，人们由 tool users 变成 tool builders。
  • 通常先做 prototype（原型）：一个早期、能运作的测试模型。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：Maker culture encourages problem-solving through DIY using raw materials and technology; a prototype is an early model to test an idea。

ex.q: A student 3D-prints a case and connects a temperature sensor to a micro:bit to make a desk fan that turns on when hot. Is this maker culture? Explain.
ex.a:
1. She has a problem (too hot at her desk).
2. She solves it herself (DIY).
3. She uses raw materials and technology (3D printing, sensor, microcontroller).
So yes, it is maker culture. Her first version is a prototype.
ex.az: 1. 有问题（太热）。2. 自己动手解决（DIY）。3. 用原材料和科技（3D 打印、传感器、微控制器）。所以是创客文化，第一版是 prototype。

ex.q: Name three technologies often used in maker projects.
ex.a:
1. Robots.
2. Electronic sensors.
3. 3D printing.
(Microcontrollers such as micro:bit / Arduino are also accepted.)
ex.az: 1. Robots 2. Electronic sensors 3. 3D printing（micro:bit、Arduino 也可以）。

ex.q: A student writes: “A prototype is the final product sold in shops.” Correct this.
ex.a:
1. This is a common mistake.
2. A prototype is not the final product.
3. It is an early, rough working model used to test an idea; makers test it, find problems and improve it before making the final product.
ex.az: 常见错误：prototype 不是最终产品，而是早期测试模型，测试后再改进。

ex.q: Tom buys a ready-made smart speaker and uses it. Is he acting as a maker?
ex.a:
1. He only uses a finished product.
2. He does not create or adapt anything.
3. So he is a tool user, not a maker (tool builder).
ex.az: 他只是使用现成产品，是 tool user，不是 maker。

cards.en:
Intuition: building a smart plant pot needs science (how plants grow), coding, building, design and maths all at once. Real problems do not stay inside one subject.

The idea: STEAM = Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, Mathematics.

  • STEAM education integrates these separate subjects.
  • Students apply them together to tackle real-life issues.
  • It builds problem-solving and innovation skills.
  • Hands-on experience is essential: you try tools, technologies and experiments, not only read.
LetterExample in a maker project
Smeasure with sensors, study the physics
Tprogram the microcontroller
Edesign the structure / circuit
Adesign the look
Mcalculate thresholds and sizes

Exam wording: STEAM education integrates Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Mathematics so students apply them to tackle real-life issues, developing problem-solving and innovation skills through hands-on experience.
cards.zh:
直觉：做一个智能花盆，要同时用到科学、编程、结构、设计和数学。真实问题不会只属于一科。

STEAM = Science、Technology、Engineering、Art、Mathematics。

  • 把原本分开的学科整合。
  • 一起应用来解决真实生活问题。
  • 培养 problem-solving and innovation skills。
  • 要有动手经验（hands-on experience）。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：STEAM education integrates the five subjects to tackle real-life issues and develop problem-solving and innovation skills through hands-on experience。

ex.q: A team builds a smart plant pot. Give one activity for each letter of STEAM.
ex.a:
1. S: study how much water and light the plant needs.
2. T: program a microcontroller to read a soil moisture sensor.
3. E: design the pump and tube system.
4. A: design an attractive pot and LED colours.
5. M: calculate the moisture threshold and water volume.
ex.az: S：植物需要多少水和光；T：编程读土壤湿度；E：设计水泵水管；A：设计外观；M：计算阈值和水量。

ex.q: What does the A in STEAM stand for? A student answers “Automation”.
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: mixing up words from this chapter.
2. A stands for Art.
3. Full form: Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, Mathematics.
ex.az: 常见错误：A 是 Art，不是 Automation。

ex.q: Why is hands-on experience important in STEAM?
ex.a:
1. Knowing facts is not enough to solve a real problem.
2. You must try different tools, technologies and experimental methods to find a working solution.
3. Testing a real prototype shows problems that theory misses.
ex.az: 只懂知识不够，要动手试不同工具和实验方法，实物测试才会发现问题。

ex.q: State the main aim of STEAM education (2 marks).
ex.a:
1. To integrate science, technology, engineering, art and mathematics (1).
2. So students apply them to tackle real-life issues and develop problem-solving and innovation skills (1).
ex.az: 整合五科（1 分）；解决真实问题、培养解难和创新能力（1 分）。

cards.en:
Intuition: you hear a question (input), think (process), then answer (output). Electronic devices work the same way.

  • Input: data the device receives via input devices (sensors, buttons).
  • Process: the methods or procedures used to process the data. Done by the processor: a programmable microcontroller in a device, the CPU in a computer.
  • Output: the responses given by the device (light, sound, text, motion).

In answers, always name all three: which sensor → what the program decides → which output device reacts.

Exam wording: Input: the [sensor] detects/measures …; Process: the microcontroller compares the reading with a threshold …; Output: the [LED/buzzer/motor] …
cards.zh:
直觉：你听到问题（输入）、想（处理）、再回答（输出）。电子设备也一样。

  • Input：通过输入设备（传感器、按钮）接收数据。
  • Process：处理数据的方法或步骤，由处理器做：设备里是 programmable microcontroller，电脑里是 CPU。
  • Output：设备的反应（光、声、文字、动作）。

答题时三部分都要写：哪个传感器 → 程序判断什么 → 哪个输出设备反应。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：Input: the [sensor] detects …; Process: the microcontroller compares the reading with a threshold …; Output: the [device] …

ex.q: Describe the IPO cycle of an automatic door.
ex.a:
1. Input: a PIR motion sensor detects a person.
2. Process: the microcontroller checks if motion is detected.
3. Output: if yes, the motor opens the door; otherwise it stays closed.
ex.az: 输入：PIR 侦测人；处理：微控制器判断有没有移动；输出：马达开门。

ex.q: Give the IPO of a smart street light.
ex.a:
1. Input: light sensor measures brightness.
2. Process: microcontroller compares brightness with a threshold.
3. Output: LED turns on if it is dark, off if bright.
ex.az: 输入：光传感器；处理：与阈值比较；输出：暗就开 LED。

ex.q: A student writes for a smart kettle: “Input: kettle. Process: heating. Output: hot water.” Why does this lose marks?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: describing the physical job, not the data flow.
2. Input must be an input device: the water temperature sensor.
3. Process must be the program's decision: compare temperature with 100°C.
4. Output must be an output device: LED / buzzer / stop the heater.
ex.az: 常见错误：写成物理过程。Input 要写输入设备（水温传感器），Process 要写程序判断（和 100°C 比较），Output 要写输出设备（LED、蜂鸣器）。

demo.title: IPO cycle of an automatic door

frames.en: A PIR motion sensor detects a person walking near.
frames.zh: PIR 传感器侦测到有人走近。

frames.en: The microcontroller runs the program: if motion detected then open.
frames.zh: 微控制器执行程序：如果侦测到移动就开门。

frames.en: The motor opens the door.
frames.zh: 马达把门打开。

frames.en: The cycle repeats again and again, so the door closes when nobody is there.
frames.zh: 周期不断重复，没人时门会关上。

cards.en:
Intuition: sensors are a device's eyes, ears and skin. Nobody needs to touch them; their reading changes automatically when the surroundings change.

Sensors are automatic input devices that read a physical quantity.

SensorMeasuresUse
Light sensor (photoresistor)light intensityautomatic lighting
Ultrasonic sensordistance (sends and receives ultrasonic waves)automatic taps, parking sensors
Temperature and humidity sensorair temperature, humiditysmart greenhouse
PIR motion sensorhuman movement (infrared)automatic doors, escalators
Accelerometer and gyroscopeacceleration, directionpedometers, drone balance
PM sensorparticulate matter concentrationair quality station

Also seen: soil moisture, pH, sound intensity, water temperature sensors.

Exam wording: Use a [name] sensor to detect/measure the [physical quantity], e.g. “an ultrasonic sensor to measure the distance between the hand and the tap”.
cards.zh:
直觉：传感器是设备的眼、耳和皮肤。不用人碰，环境一变，读数就自动改变。

Sensors 是自动输入设备，读取物理量。

传感器量度用途
Light sensor光强度自动照明
Ultrasonic sensor距离（发射和接收超声波）自动水龙头、泊车
Temperature and humidity气温、湿度智能温室
PIR motion人体移动（红外线）自动门、扶手电梯
Accelerometer/gyroscope加速度、方向计步器、无人机
PM sensor悬浮粒子浓度空气质素

Exam wording（考试这样写）：Use a [name] sensor to detect/measure the [physical quantity]。

ex.q: Choose a sensor: (a) automatic tap (b) count a runner's steps (c) smart greenhouse climate (d) air quality station.
ex.a:
(a) Ultrasonic sensor: measures distance to the hand.
(b) Accelerometer: detects each step's movement.
(c) Temperature and humidity sensor.
(d) PM sensor.
ex.az: (a) 超声波 (b) 加速度计 (c) 温湿度 (d) PM 传感器。

ex.q: A student chooses a light sensor to detect when a person walks near an automatic door. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: light changes for many reasons (clouds, lamps).
2. The correct device is a PIR motion sensor, which detects human movement by infrared radiation.
3. Match the sensor to the exact quantity: people moving → PIR.
ex.az: 常见错误：光会因很多原因改变。侦测人走近要用 PIR motion sensor。

ex.q: How does an ultrasonic sensor measure distance?
ex.a:
1. It emits an ultrasonic wave.
2. The wave hits an object and bounces back.
3. It receives the echo and uses the time taken to calculate the distance.
ex.az: 发出超声波 → 碰到物件反射 → 接收回波，用时间算距离。

ex.q: Why is a sensor called an automatic input device?
ex.a: Its data changes automatically according to changes in the environment; no person needs to adjust it.
ex.az: 数据随环境自动改变，不用人手调整。

cards.en:
Intuition: a thermometer changes by itself; a volume knob only changes when you turn it.

Automatic (sensor)Manual
Who changes the data?the environmentthe user, by hand
ExamplePIR, light sensorbutton, joystick, potentiometer
  • Button → switches, keyboards (pressed / not pressed: digital).
  • Joystick → game controllers.
  • Slide potentiometer → audio mixers, regulators.
  • Rotary potentiometer → air-conditioner temperature knob, power control.

A potentiometer gives a range of values (analogue).

Exam wording: Manual input devices require the user to adjust the data by hand, while sensors change data automatically according to the external environment.
cards.zh:
直觉：温度计自己会变；音量旋钮要你转才会变。

自动（传感器）手动
谁改变数据？环境用户用手
  • Button：开关、键盘（只有按/不按）。
  • Joystick：游戏手柄。
  • Slide potentiometer：混音台。
  • Rotary potentiometer：冷气温度旋钮。

Potentiometer 给出一个范围的数值。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：Manual input devices require the user to adjust the data by hand; sensors change automatically with the environment。

ex.q: Classify: (a) speaker volume knob (b) PIR on an escalator (c) joystick (d) PM sensor.
ex.a:
(a) Manual (rotary potentiometer).
(b) Automatic.
(c) Manual.
(d) Automatic.
Rule: if a person must adjust it, it is manual.
ex.az: (a) 手动 (b) 自动 (c) 手动 (d) 自动。

ex.q: A student says: “A button is a sensor because it detects being pressed.” Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Common mistake.
2. A button's data only changes when the user presses it by hand, so it is a manual input device.
3. A sensor reacts to the environment by itself.
ex.az: 常见错误：按钮要人手按，是 manual input device，不是传感器。

ex.q: Which device suits a fan speed control that the user can set to any level from slow to fast? Why?
ex.a:
1. A rotary (or slide) potentiometer.
2. It gives a range of values, not just on/off.
3. A button would only give two states.
ex.az: 用 potentiometer，因为它给一个范围的数值，按钮只有两种状态。

cards.en:
Intuition: output devices are how a gadget answers: it lights up, beeps, shows words or moves.

DeviceDoesUse
LEDemits light (an RGB LED can show many colours)indicator lights
Buzzeremits sounddoor bells, alarms
Displayshows informationdashboards
DC motorrotates continuously at different speedswheels, fans, water pumps
Servo motorturns to a specific anglerobot arms, wipers, doors/lids

Key rule: exact angle → servo; keep spinning → DC motor.

Exam wording: A servo motor can rotate to a specific angle; a DC motor rotates continuously at different speeds.
cards.zh:
直觉：输出设备是装置「回答」的方式：发光、发声、显示文字或移动。

设备作用用途
LED发光（RGB LED 可变色）指示灯
Buzzer发声门铃、警报
Display显示资讯仪表板
DC motor持续转动车轮、风扇、水泵
Servo motor转到指定角度机械臂、门、盖

规则：要准确角度用 servo；要一直转用 DC motor。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：A servo motor can rotate to a specific angle; a DC motor rotates continuously。

ex.q: Choose output devices: (a) automatic plant watering (b) grow light with a suitable spectrum (c) bin lid opening to 90° (d) show sensor values.
ex.a:
(a) Water pump / DC motor.
(b) RGB LED.
(c) Servo motor.
(d) Display.
ex.az: (a) 水泵/DC motor (b) RGB LED (c) servo (d) display。

ex.q: A student uses a DC motor to open a smart bin lid to exactly 90°. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake.
2. A DC motor just keeps spinning; it cannot stop at a set angle easily.
3. Use a servo motor, which rotates to a specific angle (e.g. 90°) and holds it.
ex.az: 常见错误：DC motor 会一直转，不能停在准确角度。要用 servo motor。

ex.q: A smart kettle shows red while boiling and green when done, and beeps at the end. List its output devices.
ex.a:
1. LED (red/green, or an RGB LED).
2. Buzzer for the beep.
ex.az: LED（红/绿）和 buzzer。

cards.en:
Intuition: sensors and LEDs are like hands and eyes; the microcontroller is the small brain that connects them.

  • Input and output devices are also called external / peripheral devices.
  • A programmable microcontroller is the main processor on an electronic device.
  • It is a small circuit board with various ports and pins, so you can connect different input and output devices.
  • Examples: Arduino, micro:bit, Raspberry Pi.
  • A device = hardware (board, sensors, LEDs) + software (program). You upload the program; the board then reads inputs and controls outputs.

Exam wording: A programmable microcontroller is the main processor of an electronic device; it is a small circuit board with ports and pins to connect input and output devices, and it executes the uploaded program to control them.
cards.zh:
直觉：传感器和 LED 像手和眼，微控制器是把它们连起来的小脑袋。

  • 输入和输出设备又叫 external / peripheral devices。
  • Programmable microcontroller 是电子设备的主处理器。
  • 是一块有接口和引脚（pins）的小电路板。
  • 例如 Arduino、micro:bit、Raspberry Pi。
  • 设备 = hardware + software。把程序上传后，它读取输入、控制输出。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：main processor of an electronic device; small circuit board with ports and pins; executes the uploaded program to control input/output devices。

ex.q: Trace the Arduino code when analogRead(A5) returns 350, then 520.
ex.a:
1. 350 > 400? False → digitalWrite(10, LOW) → LED off.
2. loop() repeats.
3. 520 > 400? True → digitalWrite(10, HIGH) → LED on.

ex.q: Give two examples of programmable microcontrollers and say what “pins” are for.
ex.a:
1. Examples: micro:bit, Arduino (or Raspberry Pi).
2. Pins let you connect external input and output devices (sensors, LEDs, motors) to the board.
ex.az: 例子：micro:bit、Arduino；pins 用来连接外部输入输出设备。

ex.q: A student says: “Once the sensor and LED are wired to the board, the device works.” What is missing?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: hardware alone does nothing.
2. You must write and upload a program (software).
3. The microcontroller runs the program to read the sensor and control the LED.
ex.az: 常见错误：只接好硬件不够，还要写程序并上传（software）。

notes.t: Setup function: runs once when the board starts.
notes.tz: setup 函数：开机只运行一次。

notes.t: Set pin 10 (where the LED is connected) as an output pin.
notes.tz: 把第 10 号引脚（接 LED）设为输出。

notes.t: Forever loop function: repeats until reset or power off.
notes.tz: 永久循环函数：不断重复直到重置或关机。

notes.t: Read the sensor on analogue pin A5; if the value is above 400, send HIGH to pin 10 (LED on).
notes.tz: 读取 A5 引脚的传感器；大于 400 就输出 HIGH（开灯）。

notes.t: Otherwise send LOW to pin 10 (LED off).
End of loop; it starts again from the top.
A list of sensor readings, as if read from pin A5.
notes.tz: 模拟从 A5 读到的传感器读数。

notes.t: Take each reading in turn (like the forever loop).
notes.tz: 逐个读数处理（模拟永久循环）。

cards.en:
Intuition: a security guard does not check the door once and go home; he checks again and again. Most devices must do the same.

  1. Setup function (“on start”): runs once only when the microcontroller starts. Use it to initialise variables and pins.
  2. Forever loop function: runs repeatedly until the microcontroller is reset or turned off. Put sensor checks here.

Classic bug: putting the temperature check in “on start”. At 28°C the fan turns on, but when it drops to 24°C the fan keeps running, because the program has ended. In Python we simulate the forever loop with while True: or a for loop over readings.

Exam wording: The code is in the setup / on start part, so it runs only once; the condition is never checked again. Move it into a forever loop so the sensor is read and checked repeatedly.
cards.zh:
直觉：保安不会只检查一次门就回家，而是不断巡查。设备也要这样。

  1. Setup function（on start）：开机只运行一次，用来初始化。
  2. Forever loop：不断重复，直到重置或关机。传感器检查放这里。

经典错误：把温度判断放 on start。28°C 开了风扇，降到 24°C 还在转，因为程序已结束。Python 用 while True: 或 for 模拟。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：The code is in on start, so it runs only once; move it into a forever loop so the sensor is checked repeatedly。

ex.q:
Explain why the fan never stops, and fix it.
on start
  if temperature > 25 then
    turn on fan
  else
    turn off fan
ex.a:
1. The code is in on start, so it runs only once.
2. At 28°C it turns the fan on, then the program ends.
3. Later readings (24°C) are never checked.
4. Fix: put the if…else inside forever.
ex.az: 代码在 on start，只跑一次；之后不再检查。改正：放进 forever。

ex.q: Which part should hold steps ← 0 in a pedometer, and why?
ex.a:
1. Setup / on start.
2. The counter must be set to 0 only once at the beginning.
3. If it were in forever, it would reset to 0 every time.
ex.az: 放在 on start，只需初始化一次；放 forever 会不断归零。

ex.q: Using the fixed program, what is printed for readings 28, 26, 24?
ex.a:
Loop 1: 28 > 25 → 28 fan ON
Loop 2: 26 > 25 → 26 fan ON
Loop 3: 24 > 25 False → 24 fan OFF
ex.az: 依次输出 28 fan ON、26 fan ON、24 fan OFF。

notes.t: “On start”: the program reads the temperature only once.
…turn the fan off. The program then ENDS: 26 and 24 are never checked.
notes.tz: ……关风扇。程序随即结束，26、24 都不会再检查。

notes.t: Forever loop (simulated): repeat for every new reading.
notes.tz: 模拟永久循环：每个新读数都重复。

notes.t: …fan off. 24 now turns the fan off.

code.out:
28 fan ON
26 fan ON
24 fan OFF

cards.tz: 实验：用 micro:bit 控制 LED 面板
cards.en:
Intuition: a micro:bit is a tiny computer the size of a card holder, with lights you can draw on.

  • micro:bit: about 4 cm × 5 cm, a 5 × 5 LED panel, built-in sensors and many pins.
  • Microsoft MakeCode lets you code with blocks or Python and test in a simulator.
  • Lab 8.1: countdown 3, 2, 1 in on start plays once; big heart + small heart in forever repeats like a heartbeat.

Exam wording: Code in on start runs once after the micro:bit starts; code in forever runs repeatedly, so the heartbeat animation keeps repeating.
cards.zh:
直觉：micro:bit 是卡片大小的小电脑，有可以画图的灯。

  • 约 4 cm × 5 cm，5 × 5 LED 面板、内置传感器、很多 pins。
  • MakeCode 可用积木或 Python，有 simulator。
  • Lab 8.1：3、2、1 放 on start → 只播一次；大心小心放 forever → 不断重复。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：on start runs once; forever runs repeatedly。

ex.q: What does the simulator show for the program?
ex.a:
1. On start: 3 → 2 → 1 once.
2. Forever: big heart, small heart, big heart, … repeating like a heartbeat.
ex.az: 先倒数 3、2、1 一次，然后大心小心不断交替。

ex.q: A student puts the countdown inside forever too. What changes?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: misplacing code.
2. The countdown would repeat every loop: 3, 2, 1, heart, small heart, 3, 2, 1, …
3. Code meant to run once belongs in on start.
ex.az: 常见错误：倒数放进 forever 会每次都重复。只做一次的放 on start。

ex.q: How many LEDs does the micro:bit display have? How could you test without the board?
ex.a:
1. 5 × 5 = 25 LEDs.
2. Use the MakeCode simulator in the browser.
ex.az: 25 个 LED；可用 MakeCode simulator 测试。

code.src:
basic.show_number(3)
basic.show_number(2)
basic.show_number(1)
def on_forever():
    basic.show_icon(IconNames.HEART)
    basic.show_icon(IconNames.SMALL_HEART)
basic.forever(on_forever)

notes.t: On start: show 3 on the 5×5 LED panel.
Define the function for the forever loop.
notes.tz: 定义永久循环要做的函数。

notes.t: Register the function so it repeats forever.
notes.tz: 登记函数，令它永远重复。

code.out: 3, 2, 1, then big heart / small heart / big heart / … forever

notes.t: Forever part (only 2 rounds here so it can stop).
notes.tz: forever 部分（这里只跑 2 次以便结束）。

cards.tz: 视觉化编程与文字编程
cards.en:
Intuition: LEGO bricks (visual) vs. writing an essay (textual). Bricks are easy to snap together; words let you say anything, but grammar must be right.

Visual (blocks)Textual
ExamplesScratch, MakeCode blocks, App Inventor, mBlockPython, C++, JavaScript, PHP
Howarrange blocks or flowchartswrite code line by line
Pluseasy to read and write; focus on concepts not syntaxmore flexible
Minusless flexiblemust follow strict syntax; harder for beginners

Example: the “show icon” block shows each icon for 600 ms; you can add a pause but cannot make it shorter. In Python you pass a parameter such as 200.

Exam wording: Visual programming is easy to read and write and lets beginners focus on concepts instead of syntax, but is less flexible; textual programming is more flexible but must follow strict syntax.
cards.zh:
直觉：砌积木（视觉化）对比写文章（文字）。积木容易拼；文字什么都能写，但语法要对。

VisualTextual
例子Scratch、MakeCode、App Inventor、mBlockPython、C++、JavaScript、PHP
优点易读易写，专注概念更灵活
缺点不够灵活要遵守严格语法

例：积木 show icon 默认 600 ms，不能变短；Python 可以加参数 200。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：Visual: easy to read and write, focus on concepts, less flexible; Textual: more flexible, strict syntax。

ex.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of blocks for a micro:bit heartbeat.
ex.a:
1. Advantage: easy to read and write, no syntax errors.
2. Disadvantage: less flexible; e.g. cannot show an icon for less than 600 ms.
ex.az: 优点：易读易写；缺点：不灵活，不能少于 600 ms。

ex.q: Classify: Scratch, PHP, App Inventor, C++.
ex.a:
Visual: Scratch, App Inventor.
Textual: PHP, C++.
ex.az: 视觉：Scratch、App Inventor；文字：PHP、C++。

ex.q: A student writes: “Visual programming is better because it is more flexible.” Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: swapping the pros.
2. Visual is easier, but less flexible.
3. Textual programming is the more flexible one.
ex.az: 常见错误：视觉化编程较易但较不灵活；更灵活的是文字编程。

code.src:
def on_forever():
    basic.show_icon(IconNames.HEART, 200)
    basic.show_icon(IconNames.SMALL_HEART, 200)
basic.forever(on_forever)

notes.t: Show the big heart; the extra parameter 200 sets the time to 200 ms.
notes.tz: 显示大心；参数 200 表示 200 毫秒。

notes.t: Small heart for 200 ms: faster than the block default of 600 ms.
notes.tz: 小心 200 毫秒，比积木默认 600 毫秒快。

cards.tz: 引脚与 micro:bit 内置传感器
cards.en:
Intuition: pins are like plug sockets on the board; built-in sensors are tools already in the box.

  • Pins connect external devices (LEDs, buzzers, servos, temperature and humidity sensors). Extra modules / libraries give functions to read or control pins.
Built-in inputReads
Light sensor (uses the LEDs)light level 0 (weakest) to 255 (strongest)
Temperature sensor (in the processor)°C
CompassEarth's magnetic field → direction
Accelerometeracceleration, shake, tilt
Buttons A and Bpresses

Lab 8.2: torch → reading > 100; nothing above → about 30–40.

Exam wording: The higher the ambient brightness, the larger the light level reading; the lower the brightness, the smaller the reading (range 0–255).
cards.zh:
直觉：pins 像电路板上的插座；内置传感器是盒里已有的工具。

  • Pins 连接外部设备；modules/libraries 提供读写引脚的函数。
内置输入读取
光传感器（用 LED）0 最弱 到 255 最强
温度传感器（在处理器）°C
指南针地磁场 → 方向
加速度计摇动、倾斜
按钮 A、B按下

实验：电筒照射 > 100；没遮挡约 30–40。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：higher ambient brightness → larger reading; range 0–255。

ex.q: A light reading changes from 35 to 180. What happened? What is the maximum reading?
ex.a:
1. Larger reading = brighter, so the light became brighter (e.g. a torch).
2. Maximum = 255.
ex.az: 读数变大 = 变亮；最大 255。

ex.q: Which built-in sensor would you use for (a) a step counter (b) a digital compass app (c) a room thermometer?
ex.a:
(a) Accelerometer.
(b) Compass.
(c) Temperature sensor.
ex.az: (a) 加速度计 (b) 指南针 (c) 温度传感器。

ex.q: A student says the light sensor reading of 300 means very bright. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: ignoring the range.
2. The micro:bit light level is 0 to 255, so 300 is impossible.
3. Very bright would be close to 255.
ex.az: 常见错误：范围是 0–255，不可能有 300。

ex.q: Using the code, what is printed for 35, 180, 0, 255?
ex.a:
35 → dim
180 → bright
0 → dim
255 → bright
ex.az: 35 dim、180 bright、0 dim、255 bright。

notes.t: Light levels from the micro:bit sensor (range 0 to 255).
notes.tz: micro:bit 光传感器读数（0 至 255）。

notes.t: A reading above 100 means strong light (like a torch).
notes.tz: 大于 100 表示很亮（如电筒）。

cards.en:
Intuition: a doorbell does nothing until someone presses it. Then it rings. That is an event and its response.

  • Event-driven programming: the programmer sets the event that triggers code; once the event occurs, the corresponding code (event handler) is executed.
  • Examples: press a camera shutter → take a photo; press a lift button → lift comes.
  • micro:bit: on button A pressed → show “A”; on button A+B pressed → clear screen; on shake → steps ← steps + 1.
  • Compare: a forever loop keeps checking (polling); an event handler waits until something happens.

Exam wording: When the specified event occurs (e.g. button A pressed), the corresponding event handler is executed.
cards.zh:
直觉：门铃没人按就不响，按了才响。这就是事件和反应。

  • 事件驱动程序：设定触发的事件，事件发生时执行对应代码（event handler）。
  • 例：按快门拍照；按升降机按钮。
  • micro:bit：按 A 显示 A；A+B 清屏；摇动步数加 1。
  • 对比：forever loop 不停检查；event handler 等事件发生才运行。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：When the specified event occurs, the corresponding event handler is executed。

ex.q:
Complete the pedometer.
on start
  steps ← 0
on shake
  ______
  Output steps
ex.a:
1. Missing line: steps ← steps + 1.
2. Each shake (a step) triggers the handler, adds 1 and outputs it.
ex.az: 填 steps ← steps + 1。

ex.q: What does the Python simulation print?
ex.a:
1. shake → steps 1 → prints steps 1
2. A → prints A
3. shake → prints steps 2
ex.az: 输出 steps 1、A、steps 2。

ex.q: A student puts steps ← 0 inside on shake. What happens?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake.
2. Each shake sets steps to 0, then adds 1, so it always shows 1.
3. Initialise in on start, only once.
ex.az: 常见错误：每次摇都归零再加 1，永远显示 1。初始化要放 on start。

notes.t: Event handler for the shake event.
Allow the function to change the global steps.
notes.tz: 容许函数修改全局变量 steps。
按钮 A 的处理函数。
字典：事件名 → 处理函数。

notes.t: Pretend these events happen in this order.
notes.tz: 模拟这些事件依次发生。

notes.t: Run the matching handler only when its event occurs.
notes.tz: 事件发生时才执行对应函数。

frames.en: The program waits; nothing runs until an event happens.
frames.zh: 程序在等待，没事件就不执行。

frames.en: The accelerometer detects a shake (one step).
frames.zh: 加速度计侦测到摇动（一步）。

frames.en: on shake: steps ← steps + 1 (now 1).
frames.zh: on shake：steps ← steps + 1（变 1）。

frames.en: Display shows 1, then back to waiting.
frames.zh: 显示 1，然后回到等待。

cards.en:
Intuition: a builder's spirit level has a bubble. An electronic one uses the accelerometer instead of a bubble and shows a picture on the LEDs.

  • Input: accelerometer (tilt).
  • Process: while tilt left / balanced / tilt right.
  • Output: a different pattern on the LED screen.

Tilt is the x-direction acceleration: negative = left, about 0 = balanced, positive = right. A tolerance band (−100 to 100) stops the display flickering. Watch boundaries: with strict >, exactly 100 is balanced.

Exam wording: The accelerometer detects the tilt; the microcontroller compares the x-value with the boundaries and the LED panel shows the matching pattern.
cards.zh:
直觉：普通水平仪用气泡，电子水平仪用加速度计，结果在 LED 上显示。

  • 输入：加速度计；处理：左倾/水平/右倾；输出：LED 图案。

x 负数 = 左，约 0 = 水平，正数 = 右。容差 −100 到 100 防止闪烁。注意边界：用 >，刚好 100 算水平。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：accelerometer detects tilt; compare x with boundaries; LED panel shows pattern。

ex.q: What is printed for x = −250, 40, 100, 101?
ex.a:
1. −250 < −100 → LEFT
2. 40 → BALANCED
3. 100 > 100 is False → BALANCED
4. 101 > 100 → RIGHT
ex.az: LEFT、BALANCED、BALANCED、RIGHT。

ex.q: A student says x = 100 gives RIGHT. Why is that wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake at the boundary.
2. The test is x > 100 (strictly greater).
3. 100 > 100 is False, so it falls to else → BALANCED.
ex.az: 常见错误：100 > 100 为 False，所以是 BALANCED。

ex.q: Why not use x < 0 → LEFT, x > 0 → RIGHT, else BALANCED?
ex.a:
1. The reading is never exactly 0 because of tiny shakes.
2. The display would flicker between LEFT and RIGHT.
3. A tolerance band treats small values as balanced.
ex.az: 读数很少刚好 0，会闪来闪去；用容差范围更稳定。

notes.t: Function: x is the acceleration in the x-direction.
notes.tz: 函数：x 是 x 方向的加速度。

notes.t: Much less than 0 means tilted left.
notes.tz: 远小于 0 表示向左倾。

notes.t: Much more than 0 means tilted right.
notes.tz: 远大于 0 表示向右倾。

notes.t: Print each value and its result.

cards.en:
Intuition: a rice cooker switches to “keep warm” by itself. Nobody stands next to it. That is automation.

  • Automation: the computer makes decisions on its own according to a preset program, running different instructions in different situations.
  • Examples: doors that open when someone is near, automatic taps, air-conditioners adjusting temperature.
  • Written with simple conditional statements (if…else) and relational operators (<, >, ==, <=, >=, !=), usually inside a forever loop.

Three benefits (memorise): 1. reduce manual work; 2. enhance cost-effectiveness; 3. operate continuously.

Exam wording: Automation lets a device make decisions by itself according to a preset program; it can reduce manual work, enhance cost-effectiveness and operate continuously.
cards.zh:
直觉：电饭煲煮好会自己转「保温」，不用人看着。这就是自动化。

  • Automation：电脑按预设程序自己作决定。
  • 例：自动门、自动水龙头、冷气自动调温。
  • 用 if…else 和关系运算符写，通常放在 forever loop 内。

三个好处：reduce manual work；enhance cost-effectiveness；operate continuously。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：makes decisions by itself according to a preset program; reduce manual work, enhance cost-effectiveness, operate continuously。

ex.q: State three benefits of a smart irrigation system over watering by hand.
ex.a:
1. Reduces manual work: farmers need not water every plant.
2. Cost-effective: water only when dry, saving water and labour.
3. Operates continuously: day and night, even when nobody is there.
ex.az: 减少人手、提高成本效益、持续运作。

ex.q: What does the irrigation code print for 20, 55, 30?
ex.a:
20 < 40 → 20 pump ON
55 → 55 pump OFF
30 < 40 → 30 pump ON
ex.az: 20 pump ON、55 pump OFF、30 pump ON。

ex.q: A student writes the benefit as “it is faster”. Why may this score 0?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: vague answer.
2. Use the exact points: reduce manual work, enhance cost-effectiveness, operate continuously.
3. Link it to the scenario (e.g. waters at night when farmers sleep).
ex.az: 常见错误：答得太含糊。要用指定字眼并配合情境。

notes.t: Soil moisture readings (%) over the day.
Repeat for every reading (automation runs non-stop).
notes.tz: 每个读数都重复（自动化不停运作）。

notes.t: Relational operator <: is the soil too dry?
notes.tz: 关系运算符 <：泥土太干吗？

code.out:
20 pump ON
55 pump OFF
30 pump ON

cards.en:
Intuition: you switch on the room light when it gets “too dark”. The threshold is the exact point where “too dark” starts.

  • A threshold is a boundary value used to decide what to do.
  • Street light: read the light sensor → if brightness < threshold, LED on; else LED off → repeat forever.
  • IPO: light sensor → microcontroller → LED.
  • Lab 8.4: threshold 100. Below 100 → on; 100 or above → off.
  • < or <= decides what happens exactly at the threshold. Always test boundary values.

Exam wording: The light sensor measures the brightness; if the brightness is lower than the threshold, the microcontroller turns on the LED, otherwise turns it off; this is repeated in a forever loop.
cards.zh:
直觉：太暗就开灯。阈值就是「太暗」开始的那一点。

  • Threshold 是作判断的边界值。
  • 街灯：读光传感器 → 亮度 < 阈值开灯，否则关 → 不断重复。
  • Lab 8.4：阈值 100，低于 100 开，100 或以上关。
  • < 还是 <= 决定刚好等于阈值时的结果。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：light sensor measures brightness; if lower than the threshold, turn on the LED, else off; repeated in a forever loop。

ex.q: Trace street_light for readings 30, 99, 100, 180.
ex.a:
30 → ON
99 → ON
100 < 100 False → OFF
180 → OFF
ex.az: ON、ON、OFF、OFF。

ex.q: The light must also be ON at exactly 100. Change the code.
ex.a:
1. Change level < 100 to level <= 100.
2. Now 100 → ON, 101 → OFF.

ex.q: A student writes if level > 100: return 'ON'. What goes wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: reversed comparison.
2. A larger reading means brighter, so the light would turn on in daylight and off at night.
3. Use <: dark (small reading) → ON.
ex.az: 常见错误：方向反了，白天开、晚上关。读数小 = 暗，要用 <。

notes.t: Function: level is the light sensor reading.
notes.tz: 函数：level 是光传感器读数。

notes.t: Print each reading and the result.

cards.t: Designing an automated device: smart kettle
cards.tz: 设计自动化设备：智能电热水壶
cards.en:
Intuition: design in three questions: What must I measure? → sensor. How should it react? → output devices. When? → the condition in the algorithm.

Smart kettle: red light = boiling, green = boiled; when boiled it beeps and stops.

  • Sensor: water temperature sensor.
  • Outputs: LED (red/green) and buzzer.
  • Algorithm:
    repeat
  read water temperature
  if temperature < 100 then red light
until temperature >= 100
green light; stop boiling; beep

Exam wording: Sensor: water temperature sensor to measure the water temperature. Output: LED shows the status, buzzer emits a notification sound. Algorithm: repeat reading the temperature until it reaches 100°C, then stop heating.
cards.zh:
直觉：三问：要量什么 → 传感器；怎样反应 → 输出设备；什么时候 → 算法条件。

智能水壶：红灯 = 正在煲，绿灯 = 煲好；煲好响声并停止。

  • 传感器：水温传感器。
  • 输出：LED、buzzer。
  • 算法：水温 < 100 继续煲亮红灯，直到 >= 100，然后绿灯、停止、响声。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：water temperature sensor; LED, buzzer; repeat until the temperature reaches 100°C, then stop。

ex.q: What does kettle([95, 99, 100, 101]) print?
ex.a:
1. 95 → 95 RED
2. 99 → 99 RED
3. 100 → 100 GREEN, STOP, BEEP, then break.
4. 101 is never read.
ex.az: 95 RED、99 RED、100 GREEN、STOP、BEEP，101 不会读。

ex.q: A student removes break. What is wrong with the output?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake.
2. After 100, the loop continues: 101 prints GREEN, STOP, BEEP again.
3. The kettle would beep twice. break ends the process once boiled.
ex.az: 常见错误：没有 break 会再次输出 GREEN、STOP、BEEP。

ex.q: Name the sensor and output devices for a smart bin whose lid opens when a hand is near and which beeps when full.
ex.a:
1. Sensor: ultrasonic sensor (distance to hand; another one for rubbish level).
2. Outputs: servo motor (lid angle) and buzzer.
ex.az: 超声波传感器；servo motor 和 buzzer。

notes.t: Function receives water temperatures over time.
notes.tz: 函数接收随时间的水温。

cards.en:
Intuition: a smart home is a house full of small automated helpers. For each one, ask: sensor → decision → output.

DeviceSenses / does
Smart air-conditionerindoor temperature or presence of people → on/off, speed
Smart lampuser at home / asleep → brightness and colour
Smart lockfingerprint / facial recognition, phone or watch
Smart fridgefood recognition, orders items online
Smart cooking stovetime/temperature by mobile app
Smart mirrorweather, news, outfits
Robot vacuum cleanercleans by itself
Smart home assistanttemperature, humidity, UV index → advice; voice control
Smart gardenwaters and adds nutrients
Smart Emergency Alarmdetects an elderly person's fall → calls for help

Exam wording: The [sensor] detects …; the device automatically … (e.g. “a PIR sensor detects whether someone is in the room; the air-conditioner switches off automatically when nobody is there”).
cards.zh:
直觉：智能家居就是一屋小型自动助手。每个都问：传感器 → 判断 → 输出。

智能冷气（室温/有没有人）、智能灯（在家/睡觉调亮度颜色）、智能锁（指纹/人脸）、智能雪柜（食物识别、网上订购）、智能煮食炉（手机控制）、智能镜、扫地机械人、智能家居助理（温湿度、紫外线、声控）、智能花园、紧急警报（长者跌倒求助）。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：The [sensor] detects …; the device automatically …。

ex.q: Design corridor lights that turn on when someone walks in. Give sensor, process, output.
ex.a:
1. Input: PIR motion sensor.
2. Process: if movement detected → on; if none for a set time → off.
3. Output: LED lights.
ex.az: PIR 传感器；有移动开灯，一段时间没移动关灯；LED。

ex.q: What does the smart AC code print? What if people becomes 0?
ex.a:
1. 1 > 0 and 29 > 26 → both True → AC ON.
2. people = 0 → first part False → and is False → AC OFF.
ex.az: 打印 AC ON；没人时 AC OFF。

ex.q: A student says a smart lock is safe because it uses a temperature sensor to detect the owner. Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: wrong sensor.
2. A smart lock identifies the owner by fingerprint or facial recognition (or a phone/smartwatch).
3. Temperature cannot tell people apart.
ex.az: 常见错误：智能锁用指纹或人脸识别，温度分不出人。

notes.t: Sensor data: indoor temperature 29°C, 1 person at home.
notes.tz: 传感器数据：室温 29°C，有 1 人。

notes.t: Turn on only if someone is home AND it is hot.
Both are true, so the air-conditioner turns on.

cards.t: Integrated exercise: algorithms controlling a laser cutter
cards.tz: 综合练习：激光切割机算法
cards.en:
Intuition: drawing a box on graph paper without lifting your pen. A laser cutter does the same, guided by coordinates.

  • The platform is a 2D array surface[x, y]; the nozzle moves between points while cutting.
  • A sub-program rect(x, y, w, h) cuts a w × h rectangle clockwise from the top-left (x, y):
    (x, y) → (x+w, y) → (x+w, y−h) → (x, y−h) → (x, y).
  • This uses parameters, sequence and coordinates. Reusing the sub-program avoids repeating code.

Exam wording: The sub-program uses parameters x, y, w, h; the nozzle moves to (x, y), starts cutting, moves clockwise through the corners and returns to (x, y), then stops cutting.
cards.zh:
直觉：在方格纸上一笔画一个长方形。激光切割机按坐标做同样的事。

  • 平台是 2D 数组 surface[x, y]。
  • 子程序 rect(x, y, w, h) 从左上角顺时针切：(x,y) → (x+w,y) → (x+w,y−h) → (x,y−h) → (x,y)。
  • 用到参数、顺序和坐标；重用子程序避免重复代码。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：moves to (x, y), starts cutting, moves clockwise through the corners and returns, then stops cutting。

ex.q: List the points visited by rect(2, 5, 3, 4).
A student writes the second corner as (x+w, y+h). Why is this wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake with direction.
2. Starting at the top-left and going clockwise, the next move after going right is down.
3. Down means y − h, so the point is (x+w, y−h).
ex.az: 常见错误：由左上角顺时针，向右后是向下，所以是 y − h。

ex.q: Use rect to cut two 2 × 2 squares with top-left corners (0, 4) and (5, 4).
ex.a:
1. Call rect(0, 4, 2, 2): (0,4)→(2,4)→(2,2)→(0,2)→(0,4).
2. Call rect(5, 4, 2, 2): (5,4)→(7,4)→(7,2)→(5,2)→(5,4).
3. The same sub-program is reused with different parameters.
ex.az: 调用两次 rect，参数不同即可重用。

notes.t: Sub-program: (x, y) is the top-left corner, w the width, h the height.
notes.tz: 子程序：(x, y) 是左上角，w 阔，h 高。

notes.t: The five points visited clockwise, ending back at the start.
notes.tz: 顺时针经过的五个点，最后回到起点。
切一个左上角 (2, 5)、3 × 4 的长方形。

frames.en: Move nozzle to (2, 5); start cutting.
frames.zh: 喷嘴移到 (2, 5)，开始切割。

frames.en: Back to x → (2, 1).
Back to start (2, 5); stop cutting.
frames.zh: 回到起点 (2, 5)，停止切割。

cards.en:
Intuition: normal objects (lamps, bins, air-conditioners) get a tiny “voice” on the Internet, so they can share what they sense.

  • IoT is the network of objects connected to sensors and the Internet so that data can be transferred among one another, giving up-to-date information.
  • With preset programs, they collect and process data more effectively than humans and make automatic decisions.
  • Wireless technologies: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID (Radio Frequency Identification), NFC (Near Field Communication).
  • Examples: phone GPS sees you near home → app turns on the AC; Bluetooth switch.

Exam wording: To access sensor data remotely, add a Wi-Fi module to connect the device to the Internet and program it to send real-time sensor data to the cloud.
cards.zh:
直觉：普通物件（灯、垃圾桶、冷气）在网上有了「声音」，可以分享感应到的数据。

  • IoT：物件的网络，连接传感器和互联网，互相传送数据。
  • 按预设程序，比人更有效收集处理数据并自动决定。
  • 无线技术：Wi-Fi、Bluetooth、RFID、NFC。
  • 例：GPS 知道你快到家 → 自动开冷气。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：add a Wi-Fi module to connect the device to the Internet; send real-time sensor data to the cloud。

cards.t: AIoT, big data and cloud computing
cards.tz: 人工智能物联网、大数据与云端运算
cards.en:
Intuition: IoT gives eyes everywhere; AI is the brain that learns from everything those eyes see.

  • AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things) integrates AI, big data and IoT.
  • IoT connects many devices → a massive data set called big data.
  • AI analyses big data to find trends and patterns and predict future outcomes; it can act automatically or support decisions.
  • Cloud computing gives the computing power to train AI models.

Chain: IoT collects data → big data provides samples → cloud computing trains models → AI predicts outcomes.

Exam wording: IoT collects real-time data; the data forms big data; cloud computing trains the model; AI analyses trends and patterns to predict …
cards.zh:
直觉：IoT 是到处的眼睛，AI 是从这些眼睛看到的东西学习的大脑。

  • AIoT 结合 AI、big data、IoT。
  • IoT 连接大量设备 → 海量数据 = big data。
  • AI 分析大数据，找趋势和规律，预测未来。
  • Cloud computing 提供训练模型的运算力。

流程：IoT 收集 → 大数据作样本 → 云端训练 → AI 预测。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：IoT collects data → big data → cloud computing trains → AI predicts。

ex.q: Explain how AIoT can reduce traffic congestion.
ex.a:
1. IoT: road cameras/sensors collect traffic data.
2. Data forms big data, processed by cloud computing.
3. AI finds trends and estimates journey times.
4. Apps show real-time info → drivers plan routes → less congestion.
ex.az: IoT 收集 → 大数据、云端 → AI 估算时间 → 实时资讯 → 减少塞车。

ex.q: What does the traffic code print?
ex.a:
1. Sum = 60+55+20+15 = 150; 150 ÷ 4 = 37.5 → average 37.5.
2. 37.5 < 40 → congestion: suggest another route.
ex.az: 平均 37.5，低于 40 → 输出建议改道。

ex.q: A student writes: “Cloud computing collects the data from the roads.” Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Common mistake: mixing up roles.
2. IoT sensors collect the data.
3. Cloud computing provides computing power to store/process data and train AI models.
ex.az: 常见错误：收集数据的是 IoT；云端负责运算和训练模型。

cards.en:
Intuition: teaching a child “this is a cat” with many photos. After enough examples, they can name a cat they have never seen.

  • Image recognition: AI that identifies what is in an image.
  • Lab 8.5, Google Teachable Machine, three steps:
    1. Collect samples: name each class; upload or take photos.
    2. Train the model.
    3. Test the model with new images.
  • More and more varied samples → better accuracy.
  • Output: a confidence score per class; pick the highest, reject if below a threshold.
  • Uses: smart fridge food recognition, facial recognition locks.

Exam wording: Collect samples for each class, train the model, then test the model with new images; more and more varied samples improve accuracy.
cards.zh:
直觉：用很多照片教小孩认猫，看够了就能认出没见过的猫。

  • 图像识别：辨认图片内容的 AI。
  • Teachable Machine 三步：Collect samples → Train the model → Test the model（用新图）。
  • 样本越多越多样，准确度越高。
  • 输出每类信心分数，取最高，低于阈值可拒绝。
  • 应用：智能雪柜、人脸识别锁。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：collect samples, train the model, test with new images; more varied samples improve accuracy。

ex.q: What does the predict code print?
ex.a:
1. dog 0.78 is highest and ≥ 0.6 → dog.
2. cat 0.45 is highest but < 0.6 → unknown.
ex.az: dog、unknown。

ex.q: A student tests the model only with the same photos used for training and gets 100%. Is the model good?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake.
2. The model has already seen those photos, so the result says little.
3. Test with new images not used in training to measure real accuracy.
ex.az: 常见错误：要用没用过训练的新图测试。

ex.q: A fruit model often confuses apples and tomatoes. Give two improvements.
ex.a:
1. Collect more samples of each class.
2. Use more varied samples (angles, lighting, backgrounds).
3. Retrain and test again with new images.
ex.az: 加更多、更多样的样本，再训练再测试。

code.src:
def predict(scores):
    best = max(scores, key=scores.get)
    if scores[best] < 0.6:
        return 'unknown'
    return best
print(predict({'cat': 0.15, 'dog': 0.78, 'rabbit': 0.07}))
print(predict({'cat': 0.45, 'dog': 0.40, 'rabbit': 0.15}))

notes.t: Function: scores = confidence for each class.
notes.tz: 函数：scores 是每类的信心分数。

cards.en:
Intuition: speech recognition is a typist who listens and writes down what you say. Another program then reads the words and acts.

  • Speech recognition: AI that converts human speech into text; used for voice input and voice commands (Siri, Google Assistant).
  • Lab 8.6, MIT App Inventor: Designer: add a Label, a Button and a SpeechRecognizer. Blocks: when Button1.Click → call SpeechRecognizer1.GetText; when SpeechRecognizer1.AfterGettingText → set Label1.Text to result.
  • This is event-driven. Project names must not contain spaces or Chinese characters.
  • To act, check the text for keywords.

Exam wording: Speech recognition converts human speech into corresponding text; the program then analyses the text (keywords) and performs the corresponding action.
cards.zh:
直觉：语音识别像一个听写员，把你说的写下来；另一个程序读文字后执行。

  • Speech recognition：把人声转成文字，用于语音输入和语音指令。
  • App Inventor：Label、Button、SpeechRecognizer；Button1.Click → GetText；AfterGettingText → Label1.Text = result。
  • 这是事件驱动。项目名不能有空格或中文。
  • 执行指令要找关键字。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：converts human speech into text; analyses keywords and performs the action。

2. 'light off now' → LED OFF.
3. 'open door' → UNKNOWN.

ex.q: A student deletes t = text.lower() and checks 'light on' in text. What fails?

2. 'Please turn the LIGHT ON' does not contain lower-case 'light on'.
3. It returns UNKNOWN. Convert to lower case first.

2. Code runs only when events happen (button click, text received).

cards.en:
Intuition: like cooking a new dish: find what is wrong, think of ideas, plan, cook, taste and adjust, then try again.

The engineering design process solves problems systematically; the right level of constraints helps creativity. Five steps in a cycle:

  1. Ask: point out current problems.
  2. Imagine: research and brainstorm solutions.
  3. Plan: plan precisely how to solve them.
  4. Create: build the product according to the plan.
  5. Improve: find room for improvement and repeat the whole process.

Like programming: problem definition → problem analysis → algorithm design → program development → testing and debugging.

Exam wording: Ask → Imagine → Plan → Create → Improve, and repeat the whole process to improve the product.
cards.zh:
直觉：像煮新菜：找问题、想办法、计划、动手、试味调整，再来一次。

工程设计流程系统地解决问题，适当的限制有助创意。五步循环：

  1. Ask：指出问题。
  2. Imagine：研究和脑力激荡。
  3. Plan：详细计划。
  4. Create：按计划制作。
  5. Improve：找改进空间并重复整个流程。

类似编程：problem definition → analysis → algorithm design → program development → testing and debugging。

Exam wording（考试这样写）：Ask → Imagine → Plan → Create → Improve，repeat the whole process。

ex.q: Match: (a) build the micro:bit prototype (b) notice elderly people forget to turn off the stove (c) the kettle beeps too late, adjust the code (d) brainstorm sensors.
ex.a:
(a) Create
(b) Ask
(c) Improve
(d) Imagine
ex.az: (a) Create (b) Ask (c) Improve (d) Imagine。

ex.q: A student says the process ends after Create. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Common mistake.
2. After Create comes Improve: test and find room for improvement.
3. It is a cycle: you repeat the whole process.
ex.az: 常见错误：Create 后还有 Improve，并会重复整个流程。

ex.q: Match the design steps to programming problem-solving stages: Ask, Plan, Improve.
ex.a:
1. Ask ↔ problem definition.
2. Plan ↔ algorithm design.
3. Improve ↔ testing and debugging.
ex.az: Ask ↔ 定义问题；Plan ↔ 设计算法；Improve ↔ 测试除错。

cards.en:
A robot vacuum must find its way home to its charger. Breaking the job into small sub-programs makes it easy.

  • Commands: FW (forward 1 unit), TL (turn 90° anti-clockwise), TR (turn 90° clockwise).
  • State: D = direction (0 north, 1 east, 2 south, 3 west), X, Y = horizontal and vertical distance from the charger at the top-left.
  • turnZero(): repeat TL D times, so it faces north whatever D is.
  • goZero() (facing north): FW Y times, TL (now west), FW X times.
  • goBack(): call turnZero() then goZero(). Reusing small sub-programs = modularisation.
  • Sensors: an ultrasonic sensor stops crashes (turn when the obstacle is closer than a safe distance, else keep going); a capacity sensor beeps when the dust box is nearly full.
cards.zh:
扫地机械车要自己回到充电座。拆成几个小子程序就容易写。

  • 指令：FW 前进一格；TL 逆时针转 90°；TR 顺时针转 90°。
  • 状态：D 方向（0 北、1 东、2 南、3 西），X、Y 与左上角充电座的横向、纵向距离。
  • turnZero()：TL 重复 D 次，不论原方向都转向北。
  • goZero()（面向北）：FW Y 次，TL（向西），FW X 次。
  • goBack()：先 turnZero() 再 goZero()，即模组化重用。
  • 传感器：超声波传感器防撞（距离小于安全距离就转向，否则前进）；容量传感器在尘盒快满时发声提示。

ex.q: D = 3 (west). How many TL does turnZero() do, and does it end facing north?
ex.a: 3 TL: west → south → east → north. Yes.
ex.az: 3 次 TL：西→南→东→北。

ex.q: D = 0, X = 2, Y = 1. List goZero()'s commands.
ex.a: FW, TL, FW, FW.
ex.az: FW、TL、FW、FW。

ex.q: Ada writes goZero() with TR after moving up. What goes wrong?
ex.a: Wrong: facing north, TR turns to the east, away from the charger on the left. It must be TL (to the west).
ex.az: 错：面向北时 TR 会转向东，离开左边的充电座，应用 TL。

notes.t: TL D times always ends facing north.
notes.tz: TL 做 D 次一定面向北。

code.out: TL TL FW FW FW TL FW FW FW FW

cards.t: Integrated exercise: cinema seats, 2D array vs three arrays
cards.tz: 综合练习：戏院座位，2D 数组 vs 三个数组
cards.en:
Two ways to record sold cinema seats: a full seating map, or a short list of who bought what.

  • 2D array seat[i,j]: rows i = 1..5 (A–E), seats j = 1..8. Sold seat stores its label (e.g. seat[3,2] = C2); unsold stores 0.
  • sold(): nested loops over all 5 × 8 cells, count cells != 0.
  • Three parallel arrays row, col, name: record i is row[i], col[i], name[i] (needed for real-name tickets).
  • check(r, c): linear search 1 to sold(); if row[i] = r and col[i] = c, return name[i]; else "None".
  • Advantage of three arrays: less storage when fewer than 5 × 8 seats are sold. Disadvantage: finding a seat needs a search (slower); operations are more complicated.
cards.zh:
记录已售座位有两种方法：完整座位图，或一张谁买了哪个座位的清单。

  • 2D 数组 seat[i,j]：i = 1..5（A–E 行），j = 1..8。已售存座位编号（如 seat[3,2] = C2），未售存 0。
  • sold()：嵌套循环走遍 5 × 8 格，数 != 0 的格。
  • 三个平行数组 row、col、name：第 i 项是 row[i]、col[i]、name[i]（实名购票需要）。
  • check(r, c)：由 1 到 sold() 线性检索；row[i] = r 且 col[i] = c 就传回 name[i]，否则 "None"。
  • 三个数组优点：售出少于 5 × 8 时占较少空间。缺点：找某座位要检索（较慢），操作较复杂。

ex.q: Seats C2, C3, C5, D4, D5, E6, E7 are sold. Give seat[3,5], seat[5,3], seat[4,5].
Complete sold(): total ← 0; for i 1 to 5; for j 1 to 8; if ___ then total ← total + 1.
ex.a: seat[i,j] != 0.
ex.az: 条件是 seat[i,j] != 0。

ex.q: Ben says three arrays are always better because they are smaller. Is he right?
ex.a: No. They are smaller only when few seats are sold. Finding who sits at seat[r,c] now needs a linear search, so it is slower than reading seat[r,c] directly.
ex.az: 错：只有售出少时才较省空间；找某座位要线性检索，比直接读 seat[r,c] 慢。

cards.tz: 综合练习：fromMin / fromMax 检索
cards.en:
If a list is sorted, you can stop early, and you can start from the closer end.

  • fromMin(num): linear search left to right. Faster: while i <= 6 AND num >= winner[i], so it stops once items are bigger than num.
  • fromMax(num): right to left: i ← 6, while i >= 1 AND num <= winner[i], i ← i − 1.
  • Combined: if target ≤ winner[3] use fromMin, else fromMax. This halves the search range, so fewer comparisons on average.
  • In a singly linked list, fromMax is hard because you cannot go back to the previous node. Fix: add a pointer to the previous node (doubly linked list).
  • Binary search does not help on a linked list: it needs direct access, but a linked list only allows sequential access.
  • Linked list advantage: insert/delete only changes pointers; an array must move items one by one.
cards.zh:
列表已排序时，可以提早停止，也可以由较近的一端开始找。

  • fromMin(num)：由左至右线性检索。改良：while i <= 6 AND num >= winner[i]，遇到较大的项就停。
  • fromMax(num)：由右至左：i ← 6，while i >= 1 AND num <= winner[i]，i ← i − 1。
  • 合并：target ≤ winner[3] 用 fromMin，否则用 fromMax，检索范围减半，平均比较次数较少。
  • 单向链表难写 fromMax，因为不能回到前一个节点；可加指向前一节点的指针（双向链表）。
  • 链表不能用二分检索提升效率：二分检索要直接存取，链表只能顺序存取。
  • 链表优点：插入/删除只改指针；数组要逐项移动。

ex.q: winner = 158 161 168 170 173 178. With the improved fromMin, how many items are checked when searching 165?
ex.a: 158, 161, 168: at 168 the condition 165 ≥ 168 is false, so it stops after checking 3 items (2 full comparisons inside the loop).
ex.az: 检查 158、161，到 168 条件不成立而停止。

ex.q: Complete fromMax: i ← 6; while i >= 1 AND ___; if num = winner[i] return True; i ← ___.
ex.a: num <= winner[i]; i − 1.
ex.az: num <= winner[i]；i − 1。

ex.q: Chris says: store the winners in a linked list and use binary search to make it faster. Reply.
ex.a: Wrong: binary search needs direct access to the middle item; a linked list only allows sequential access, so it cannot jump to the middle.
ex.az: 错：二分检索要直接存取中间项，链表只能顺序存取。

notes.t: Stop early once items are bigger than num.
notes.tz: 遇到较大项就提早停止。

cards.t: Integrated exercise: stack export(L) with a second stack
cards.tz: 综合练习：用第二个 stack 的 export(L)
cards.en:
To take some boxes out of the middle of a pile but keep the rest in order, unpile onto a second pile, then pile them back.

  • Operations: push(S, L), pop(S), isEmpty(S).
  • export(L): pop every item from box; if it is not L, push it onto out. Then pop everything from out back onto box.
  • The second stack reverses the order twice, so the kept items end up in their original order.
  • Tracing push/pop: pop removes the top (highest index); push adds after it.
while not isEmpty(box)
  temp ← pop(box)
  if temp != L then push(out, temp)
while not isEmpty(out)
  push(box, pop(out))
cards.zh:
要从一叠箱子中间取走部分，又要其余保持次序：先逐个搬到另一叠，再搬回来。

  • 操作：push(S, L)、pop(S)、isEmpty(S)。
  • export(L)：从 box 逐项 pop；不是 L 就 push 到 out。之后把 out 全部 pop 回 box。
  • 第二个 stack 令次序倒转两次，剩下的项回到原来次序。
  • 追踪：pop 取走顶部（最大 index）；push 放在顶部之后。
while not isEmpty(box)
  temp ← pop(box)
  if temp != L then push(out, temp)
while not isEmpty(out)
  push(box, pop(out))

ex.q: box (bottom→top) = HK HK KLN NT. Do pop, push NT, push NT, pop, push KLN, push HK.
ex.a: HK HK KLN NT KLN HK.
ex.az: HK HK KLN NT KLN HK。

ex.q: box = KLN NT KLN NT KLN NT HK HK. Result of export(NT)?
ex.a: KLN KLN KLN HK HK.
ex.az: KLN KLN KLN HK HK。

ex.q: Ada skips the second loop and leaves the kept items in out. Why is that wrong?
ex.a: Wrong: the items would be in the wrong stack and in reversed order. Moving them back to box reverses them again into the original order.
ex.az: 错：项目留在 out 且次序倒转；搬回 box 才回到原次序。

notes.t: Keep items that are not L.
notes.tz: 保留不是 L 的项。

cards.t: Integrated exercise: storing an image in a text file (run-length)
cards.tz: 综合练习：用文本文件储存图像（连续编码）
cards.en:
Instead of writing "white, white, white, white", you can write "white × 4". That is the idea of Method 2.

  • Pixels: 0 white, 1 grey, 2 black.
  • Method 1: one digit per pixel; its position in the file = its position in the image.
  • Method 2: scan top to bottom, left to right; each run of the same digit is stored as [D,N] (digit, number of times in a row). Runs can carry over to the next row.
  • Method 2 file size: best case all pixels the same colour; worst case no two neighbouring pixels the same (bigger than Method 1).
  • Method 1 advantages: simpler; quicker to turn into a 2D array.

image = ["22221", "11000", "00000", "11112", "22222"]
def encode(rows):
    pixels = "".join(rows)          # scan top-bottom, left-right
    groups = []
    d, n = pixels[0], 1
    for p in pixels[1:]:
        if p == d:
            n += 1
        else:
            groups.append([int(d), n]); d, n = p, 1
    groups.append([int(d), n])
    return groups

cards.en:
The book ends Elective C with game projects that combine everything: 2D arrays, loops, sub-programs and input checks.

  • Connect Four: 6 × 7 2D array; a disc drops to the lowest empty cell in a column; check 4 in a row horizontally, vertically and diagonally; draw if the board fills. Variant: two human players instead of player vs computer.

  • Mastermind: guess 4 coloured pegs in 10 turns; black peg = right colour and position, white peg = right colour, wrong position.
